newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Nobel laureate urges Indonesia troop cut in E.Timor.
newsitem.headline: Nobel laureate urges Indonesia troop cut in E.Timor.

text.p: Nobel Peace prize laureate Jose Ramos Horta, a campaigner for self-determination for East Timor, said Monday Indonesian troops in the territory should be reduced to fewer than 1,000 and confined to barracks.
He also urged an end to armed activities by East Timorese "resistance fighters" and establishment of a zone where they and their families could assemble under international protection.
Ramos Horta was addressing the U.N. decolonization committee before the foreign ministers of Indonesia and Portugal hold talks at the United Nations on June 19-20.

Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 after Portugal withdrew from its former colony, and annexed it the following year. Guerrillas of the Fretilin independence movement continued for years to mount attacks on Indonesian troops.
Human rights groups said up to one-third of the population, or about 200,000 people, died during the invasion and subsequent fighting and famine in East Timor.
The international community does not recognise the annexation, and U.N.-sponsored talks between Portugal and Indonesia to find a solution have dragged on since 1983.

Referring to a recent escalation of violence in East Timor, Ramos Horta said: "Indonesian troop presence in East Timor must be reduced to a minimal level, equivalent for instance to the Portuguese troop level in East Timor in 1974, which never exceeded 1,000."
There were fewer than 500 in 1975, in the course of the decolonization process, he added.

He did not say how many Indonesian troops were now stationed in the territory. A recent U.N. report quoted Indonesian sources for a figure of about 3,000 at the end of 1996 but said other sources estimated the number at between 7,000 and 10,000.
"Indonesian remaining troops should be confined to their barracks," Ramos Horta said.

"East Timorese resistance fighters should observe a cessation of all armed activities. A protection zone should be created in an agreed region of East Timor where the armed resistance forces and their families can assemble under international humanitarian protection.
"Prisoners should be released. Torture must end. A representative office of the U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights should be established in East Timor."
Ramos Horta, who shared the 1996 Nobel Peace prize with Bishop Carlos Ximenes Belo of East Timor, said such an office could help the local people and authorities communicate.

"East Timorese should be given the right to govern their own country," Ramos Horta said, citing as examples of autonomy the Portugese territories of Azores, Madeira and Macau, the Basque country in Spain and the Cook Islands, a self-governing New Zealand territory.
A decision on the legal status of East Timor should be made later, he said, without giving a time frame.
